messages.subject_clean: question about one of the examples in your vignette.
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
out of curiosity, I've been trying to reproduce the following commands from your vignette, displaying the values of "length_0.95_HPD" from a Beast tree.  <https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/ggtree/inst/doc/treeImport.html#parsing-beast-output>

ggtree(beast, ndigits=2, branch.length = 'none') + geom_text(aes(x=branch, label=length_0.95_HPD), vjust=-.5, color='firebrick')

It doesn't work anymore, as I think that there have been some changes in your package. I'm curious as to how you could get it to work, as I'm in the process of learning how to use ggtree.

This is the error message I get.
> ggtree(tre3, branch.length = 'none') + geom_text(aes(x=branch, label=length_0.95_HPD), vjust=-.5, color='firebrick')
Don't know how to automatically pick scale for object of type list. Defaulting to continuous.
Error in (function (..., row.names = NULL, check.rows = FALSE, check.names = TRUE,  :
  les arguments impliquent des nombres de lignes différents : 383, 2

Thanks in advance,
Edeline

messages.subject: Add informations on edge
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I am sorry but I am meeting a dead-end here. I draw a tree and I have a data frame with the “position” of mutations, i.e. the branches where they should be. I would like to add points on my tree according to these mutations. I have different issues but it works approximatively. My real problem is that the points having the same parent and node information (i.e. the points supposed to be on the same branch) are not all represented, only one is, but not the others. I tried to put transparency as suggested in the help of the geom_point function to check if points are superimposed but no, there is indeed only one point.
I join an example of my data and a plot for more clarity with my code ( cf PJ).

As you can see on the line 1 and 4  of my data frame I have the same info, I hope to plot two points on the edge but I have only one, the point corresponding to the first line.
Does anyone have any ideas or suggestions to help me?

(I tried to make a loop, I check geom_subview but I do not want pie chart, I really search solutions before ask your help)

Thank you so much
Marie

messages.subject: Re: Plot the same tree side by side?
messages.subject_clean: Plot the same tree side by side?
messages.body_plain:
Hello, again,

Is there any way to reduce the gap between plots more? The best I have been able to do is remove the margin on the plots. See below:

library(ggtree)
library(cowplot)

# create random tree
set.seed(123)
tree <- rtree(30)

# plot tree
p = ggtree(tree, branch.length = "none")

# plot same tree side by side
p1 = p + geom_tiplab(hjust = 0.5, offset = 0.9) + ggplot2::theme(plot.margin = margin(0,0,0,0, unit = "mm"))
p2 = p + scale_x_reverse() + ggplot2::theme(plot.margin = margin(0,0,0,0, unit = "mm"))

cowplot::plot_grid(p1, p2, ncol=2)

Also, I am unable to plot pie charts on the nodes of the reversed tree.

For example the code below results in the attached tree

# make data for pie charts
A = runif(29)
B = 1 - A
data = data.frame(node, A, B)
data

pies <- nodepie(data, cols = 2:3)

inset(p2, pies)

Apologies if I have missed something simple!

Cheers
Ollie
